First of all, the Minix Mini Dishwasher Pro 3-Person arrived quickly. However, when I tried to open it, the box was delivered upside down. There was a sponge stuck inside the box, so there was no defect in the product, but I wasn't very happy about it. I thought it would be small because it's mini, but it was a bit bulky when I received it. It's not easy for a woman to lift alone, but it's a size and weight that I can carry. The color is charcoal gray, and I really liked it because it matches the water purifier in my house. However, the dust was easily visible, so I thought I'd have to cover it with something. My kitchen is mostly dark, so this was perfect. Installation wasn't that difficult. Just put the water tank up, attach the accessories to the end, and place the main unit on top of it. After that, you just need to properly connect the drain hose to the back of the main unit and you're done. If you pull the hose out to the side toward the dishwasher, the water will drain there whenever you use it. I think the biggest advantage is that it can be installed without drilling. One of the disadvantages is that you have to find a place to put it, such as a sink, but I think it can be done. And the instruction booklet is very detailed and explains where and what to put the dishes. It looks nice. The interior has a two-tiered tray structure. You can put plates, bowls, cups, etc. on the bottom, and spoons and cooking utensils on the top. It doesn't hold as many dishes as you might think because it's small. But I think this is okay for me. If you arrange it well, it will be okay. I recommend it for a one- or two-person household. I think it can be used by up to three people without any problems. I have a tornado rotating blade on the top and bottom of the interior. Here. The water stream is quite powerful, and you can fill it by pulling the water tank inlet at the bottom. Another disadvantage is that it has to be filled every time it is used, perhaps because it is a mini. However, it is designed to hold up to 7-8 liters, so it seems to run once or twice without any problems. When there is no water, the product itself makes a "beep" sound. When you fill it with water, the product displays "full" and you can stop. After larvae are removed and the dishes with fishy smells are put in and the dishwasher is running, all the smells are gone and it comes out dry, which is great. The advantage is that there are no installation space restrictions and no need to connect a drain pipe. However, the manual method of adding water is a bit inconvenient. The detergent is added. At first, I was told to put it in the area with writing on the bottom, but after searching for a while, I found a stainless steel area around the water source. I just placed it there. It was easy. The Minix dishwasher has six modes to choose from: Economy, Standard, Powerful, Quick, Internal Wash, and Dry. Yes, I often use the standard mode. And it's a small, multi-functional dishwasher that not only washes, but also sterilizes and dries. First of all, the Minix Mini Dishwasher Pro 3-Person arrived quickly. However, when I tried to open it, the box was delivered upside down. There was a sponge stuck inside the box, so there was no defect in the product, but I wasn't very happy about it. I thought it would be small because it's mini, but it was a bit bulky when I received it. It's not easy for a woman to lift alone, but it's a size and weight that I can carry. The color is charcoal gray, and I really liked it because it matches the water purifier in my house. However, the dust was easily visible, so I thought I'd have to cover it with something. My kitchen is mostly dark, so this was perfect. Installation wasn't that difficult. Just put the water tank up, attach the accessories to the end, and place the main unit on top of it. After that, you just need to properly connect the drain hose to the back of the main unit and you're done. If you pull the hose out to the side toward the dishwasher, the water will drain there whenever you use it. I think the biggest advantage is that it can be installed without drilling. One of the disadvantages is that you have to find a place to put it, such as a sink, but I think it can be done. And the instruction booklet is very detailed and explains where and what to put the dishes. It looks nice. The interior has a two-tiered tray structure. You can put plates, bowls, cups, etc. on the bottom, and spoons and cooking utensils on the top. It doesn't hold as many dishes as you might think because it's small. But I think this is okay for me. If you arrange it well, it will be okay. I recommend it for a one- or two-person household. I think it can be used by up to three people without any problems. I have a tornado rotating blade on the top and bottom of the interior. Here. The water stream is quite powerful, and you can fill it by pulling the water tank inlet at the bottom. Another disadvantage is that it has to be filled every time it is used, perhaps because it is a mini. However, it is designed to hold up to 7-8 liters, so it seems to run once or twice without any problems. When there is no water, the product itself makes a "beep" sound. When you fill it with water, the product displays "full" and you can stop. After larvae are removed and the dishes with fishy smells are put in and the dishwasher is running, all the smells are gone and it comes out dry, which is great. The advantage is that there are no installation space restrictions and no need to connect a drain pipe. However, the manual method of adding water is a bit inconvenient. The detergent is added. At first, I was told to put it in the area with writing on the bottom, but after searching for a while, I found a stainless steel area around the water source. I just placed it there. It was easy. The Minix dishwasher has six modes to choose from: Economy, Standard, Powerful, Quick, Internal Wash, and Dry. Yes, I often use the standard mode. And it's a small, multi-functional dishwasher that not only washes, but also sterilizes and dries. When you're concerned about residual moisture or unpleasant odors from stacking dishes, you can use the drying function, which dries the dishes thoroughly for 1 hour and 20 minutes. It even sterilizes and deodorizes them. I'm satisfied because I can manage my kitchen utensils hygienically by using the drying function without having to sterilize them separately. At first, I was worried that it might be noisy if I ran it at night, but the Minix is **designed for low noise**, so it's much quieter than I thought. But it would be noisy at night, right? Of course, I wouldn't run it too late at night. There's the sound of running water and a slight fan during the wash, but it's enough to ignore while watching TV or listening to music. Dishwashers are often expensive, but the Minix is "reasonably priced," so even single-person households, young adults, and those living alone can afford it without too much of a burden. It has many reviews saying that it offers good value for money compared to similar compact dishwashers, and it comes with a dedicated detergent, so you don't have to worry about additional costs.

Comments (English): [ This dishwasher is better than I expected! ] || ---------------- || This is a review I wrote after receiving a free product as part of a Coupang Experience Group event. This was actually my first time using this brand, but my husband said he'd heard a lot about it. So I was skeptical about buying it, but after receiving it and using it, I found it to be more than satisfactory. First of all, it's absolutely beautiful! The luxurious exterior makes it look much more substantial than its price range suggests, making it a perfect fit for the term "value-for-money dishwasher." It's perfect for single- or two-person households! I usually prefer ivory or white-toned appliances, but this time I chose charcoal gray. When I received it, it felt subtly sophisticated and luxurious, making it a perfect addition to my kitchen. It's matte, but it's really pretty. It's actually larger than I expected. I was surprised by the size of the delivery box, but thanks to that, it can hold quite a lot of dishes. It's big enough for small plates and cups, and even small pots and pans can be washed. The two-tier interior gives it ample storage space, and it's actually quite practical. The buttons are simple, so I was able to use it after just a few glances at the manual. The drain hose is long enough that I can install it and cut it to fit my home's layout. Usually, dishwashers require scheduling a technician's visit and drilling holes in the sink, which is a hassle. But this one was much more convenient because I could just have it delivered and install it myself. I was satisfied because I could use it as soon as I found the space, and there was no complicated installation process required. I wanted to connect it directly to the water supply, but that would have required purchasing separate parts, so I gave up. The cleaning power exceeded my expectations. I was worried that the small size might compromise cleaning power, but it's actually powerful and was able to clean even food stains thoroughly. The key is to stack Tetris correctly. With a baby coming soon, I really wanted a small dishwasher, and the size is perfect, along with its powerful cleaning power, which put my mind at ease. This product truly embodies the phrase "small but mighty." One downside is that there aren't many detergents specifically designed for three-person dishes. Minix detergent is the best option, but the price seems a bit high. If you're using a regular dishwasher, you'll need to cut it in half. Sentence (English): The design isn't overly flashy, and it goes well with our cream-colored sink.
Comments (English): [ It seems like a dishwasher that costs just that much. ] || ---------------- || The design isn't overly flashy, and it goes well with our cream-colored sink. I also like that I don't have to worry about filter maintenance like with the Samsung. The installer was very friendly. I told the sink company the size and model and made a reservation, but the installer said it didn't fit, so I thought he wouldn't be able to install it, but he handled it well. We're a family of four, and the kids are still babies, so they don't have a lot of dishes, so we usually cook two or three meals at a time. Since it's for 14 people, it's really big, so we have to do three meals at a time to fill it up. It even fits pots and cooking bowls! After installation, they told me how to lower the basket and other things, but I don't remember them. I'm using it because it's convenient, and I'll look into it later. It has a hot air dryer, steam, and sterilization function, making it convenient for managing children's dishes in the summer. (I don't use it every time due to electricity bills.) I even spin the baby bottles in the sink. There's no separate rinse function on the device itself; you can download it to your phone. There are a lot of downloadable programs. It would be nice if there was a soaking function, but it's a bit disappointing. The steam function of the dishwasher is a bit burdensome. And you have to do this a few times to clean it thoroughly. There's a cleaning program for stuck-on food burns in the LG ThinQ app, but I don't bother using it. I used a stand-alone dishwasher before, so the extra washing isn't that inconvenient. Oh, and the touch buttons don't work well when my hands get wet. But this one also has a strange food smell inside the dishwasher, just like the stand-alone model. The stand-alone model I used before was like that, so I thought it was because it was a stand-alone model, but this one has the same smell. There was no food stuck in the mesh, so I'm going to give it a thorough cleaning tomorrow to see what the problem is. I bought it with high expectations, but it wasn't as good as I imagined.---------After adding vinegar and doing a thorough cleaning, the smell went away!

Sentence (English): The design isn't too flashy, and for starters, it matches well with cream-colored sinks.
Comments (English): [ It seems like a dishwasher that is just about what you'd expect for the price. ] || ---------------- || The design isn't too flashy, and for starters, it matches well with cream-colored sinks. I like that I don't have to go through the hassle of filter maintenance like with SamO. The installation technician was incredibly kind. I had the cabinets custom-built after providing the size and model to the sink manufacturer, and I initially thought they wouldn't be able to install it because the technician said it wouldn't fit, but they managed to get it done well somehow. We are a family of four, and since the kids are still babies, we don't produce a lot of dishes, so we tend to cook two or three meals a day at once. Since it's a 14-place setting, it's really big, so it fills up completely only when we do three meals in a row. Pots and bowls fit inside! After installation, they explained things like how to lower the basket and other details, but I don't remember them all. I'm just using it because there are no inconveniences, and I plan to look them up later. It features hot air drying, steam, and sterilization functions, making it convenient to manage the kids' dishes in the summer (though I don't use them every time due to electricity costs). I even run the baby bottles along with the dishes. There isn't a standalone rinse function on the unit itself, but you have to download a guide on your phone to use it. There are many courses available for downloading and use. It would have been nice if there were a soaking function, so that is a bit of a shame. The dishwasher's steam function is a bit too much of a hassle. Also, you need to do a preliminary wash to get it cleaned properly. There is a cleaning course for burnt-on food in the LG ThinQ app, but I don't really go that far with it. Since I used a freestanding dishwasher before, the preliminary wash isn't a major inconvenience. Oh, and the touch buttons don't work well if my hands get wet. However, just like the freestanding model, there is a strange smell coming from inside the dishwasher—I'm not sure if it's because it's a freestanding type. The freestanding model I used before had the same smell, so I wondered if it was because it was a freestanding model, but this one is the same. There was no food stuck in the mesh, so I'm not sure where the problem is; I plan to try a drum clean tomorrow. I bought this with high expectations, but it was a dishwasher that wasn't much better than I imagined. ---------. The smell disappeared after I put in vinegar and ran a drum clean!

Sentence (English): With three kids, a single meal results in a mountain of dishes!
Comments (English): [ A mom of three's escape from dishwashing hell! Samsung 6-person dishwasher, you are my destiny. ] || ---------------- || With three kids, a single meal results in a mountain of dishes! When you add up the trays, spoons, chopsticks, and water cups, it is literally a dishwashing hell. I used to use a Cuckoo 3-place dishwasher, but it broke down, so I did the dishes by hand for a while—I actually shed a few tears back then. (The repair cost was about the same as buying a new one.) A large 12-place model was too much of a burden, so I was looking for just the right size for 6 and managed to snag it for the mid-400,000 won range thanks to a credit card discount! Cleaning power? No pre-washing, just cleanliness. I'm too lazy to pre-wash, so I usually just rinse them quickly with water and put them in. But this thing really cleaned everything so thoroughly that I was amazed. Even soup stains and rice residue vanished completely! You just put in the detergent tablets, and it takes care of everything automatically, so it feels like a smart housekeeping assistant. Automatic door opening = a whole new world experience. When it's finished, the door pops open automatically to let the moisture escape and even air dry! Wow, this is a whole new world feature that only those who have used it truly understand. It's subtly stressful when you finish washing dishes but they aren't completely dry, but with this one, that worry is zero. There are higher-end models that even feature hot air drying, but I'm not so sure about that. The reason it's more convenient is that it's a 6-place setting. With the large 12-place setting, you have to wait for it to fill up, so it feels like you're dumping all the dishes in at once, but with the 6-place model, you can start it right after finishing a meal. For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. Since it's beige, it looks subtly luxurious in the kitchen. It's simple and not flashy, so it doesn't ruin the interior. It has that perfect "clean kitchen item" vibe. My husband even complimented it, saying the kitchen looks prettier now that we have this. Oh, right, and why is it so quiet? The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" But the Samsung dishwasher is so quiet that I find myself constantly checking to see if it's even working. Total summary of pros. Great cleaning power (no pre-washing needed). The automatic door opening and drying function is a game changer. Since it's a 6-place setting, it's great to run it right after every meal. The design is sleek and doesn't ruin the interior. Honestly, there are some downsides. Large pots and pans still need to be hand-washed. (But we use a huge 30-inch frying pan, so it would probably be a bit awkward to fit that in a 12-place setting anyway.) The amount you can put in at once is limited compared to the 12-place setting. There is a rinse aid dispenser, but it's useless to me since I use tablet detergent. Conclusion = Definitely a holy grail item. They say there are people who have never used a dishwasher, but there are no people who have only used one once. Yes, that is exactly me. When you add up the trays, spoons, chopsticks, and water cups, it is literally a dishwashing hell. I used to use a Cuckoo 3-place dishwasher, but it broke down, so I did the dishes by hand for a while—I actually shed a few tears back then. (The repair cost was about the same as buying a new one.) A large 12-place model was too much of a burden, so I was looking for just the right size for 6 and managed to snag it for the mid-400,000 won range thanks to a credit card discount! Cleaning power? No pre-washing, just cleanliness. I'm too lazy to pre-wash, so I usually just rinse them quickly with water and put them in. But this thing really cleaned everything so thoroughly that I was amazed. Even soup stains and rice residue vanished completely! You just put in the detergent tablets, and it takes care of everything automatically, so it feels like a smart housekeeping assistant. Automatic door opening = a whole new world experience. When it's finished, the door pops open automatically to let the moisture escape and even air dry! Wow, this is a whole new world feature that only those who have used it truly understand. It's subtly stressful when you finish washing dishes but they aren't completely dry, but with this one, that worry is zero. There are higher-end models that even feature hot air drying, but I'm not so sure about that. The reason it's more convenient is that it's a 6-place setting. With the large 12-place setting, you have to wait for it to fill up, so it feels like you're dumping all the dishes in at once, but with the 6-place model, you can start it right after finishing a meal. For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. Since it's beige, it looks subtly luxurious in the kitchen. It's simple and not flashy, so it doesn't ruin the interior. It has that perfect "clean kitchen item" vibe. My husband even complimented it, saying the kitchen looks prettier now that we have this. Oh, right, and why is it so quiet? The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" But the Samsung dishwasher is so quiet that I find myself constantly checking to see if it's even working. Total summary of pros. Great cleaning power (no pre-washing needed). The automatic door opening and drying function is a game changer. Since it's a 6-place setting, it's great to run it right after every meal. The design is sleek and doesn't ruin the interior. Honestly, there are some downsides. Large pots and pans still need to be hand-washed. (But we use a huge 30-inch frying pan, so it would probably be a bit awkward to fit that in a 12-place setting anyway.) The amount you can put in at once is limited compared to the 12-place setting. There is a rinse aid dispenser, but it's useless to me since I use tablet detergent. Conclusion = Definitely a holy grail item. They say there are people who have never used a dishwasher, but there are no people who have only used one once. Yes, that is exactly me. Now that I'm freed from hand washing, my quality of life has truly improved. I can play with the kids or have a cup of coffee while it runs; for me, it's the best parenting and housekeeping item! Overall: A realistic size perfect for a mom + powerful cleaning power + a pretty design. Highly recommended! [[[The 'Helpful' button makes me so excited]]]

When you add up the trays, spoons, chopsticks, and water cups, it is literally a dishwashing hell. I used to use a Cuckoo 3-place dishwasher, but it broke down, so I did the dishes by hand for a while—I actually shed a few tears back then. (The repair cost was about the same as buying a new one.) A large 12-place model was too much of a burden, so I was looking for just the right size for 6 and managed to snag it for the mid-400,000 won range thanks to a credit card discount! Cleaning power? No pre-washing, just cleanliness. I'm too lazy to pre-wash, so I usually just rinse them quickly with water and put them in. But this thing really cleaned everything so thoroughly that I was amazed. Even soup stains and rice residue vanished completely! You just put in the detergent tablets, and it takes care of everything automatically, so it feels like a smart housekeeping assistant. Automatic door opening = a whole new world experience. When it's finished, the door pops open automatically to let the moisture escape and even air dry! Wow, this is a whole new world feature that only those who have used it truly understand. It's subtly stressful when you finish washing dishes but they aren't completely dry, but with this one, that worry is zero. There are higher-end models that even feature hot air drying, but I'm not so sure about that. The reason it's more convenient is that it's a 6-place setting. With the large 12-place setting, you have to wait for it to fill up, so it feels like you're dumping all the dishes in at once, but with the 6-place model, you can start it right after finishing a meal. For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. Since it's beige, it looks subtly luxurious in the kitchen. It's simple and not flashy, so it doesn't ruin the interior. It has that perfect "clean kitchen item" vibe. My husband even complimented it, saying the kitchen looks prettier now that we have this. Oh, right, and why is it so quiet? The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" But the Samsung dishwasher is so quiet that I find myself constantly checking to see if it's even working. Total summary of pros. Great cleaning power (no pre-washing needed). The automatic door opening and drying function is a game changer. Since it's a 6-place setting, it's great to run it right after every meal. The design is sleek and doesn't ruin the interior. Honestly, there are some downsides. Large pots and pans still need to be hand-washed. (But we use a huge 30-inch frying pan, so it would probably be a bit awkward to fit that in a 12-place setting anyway.) The amount you can put in at once is limited compared to the 12-place setting. There is a rinse aid dispenser, but it's useless to me since I use tablet detergent. Conclusion = Definitely a holy grail item. They say there are people who have never used a dishwasher, but there are no people who have only used one once. Yes, that is exactly me. Now that I'm freed from hand washing, my quality of life has truly improved. I can play with the kids or have a cup of coffee while it runs; for me, it's the best parenting and housekeeping item! Overall: A realistic size perfect for a mom + powerful cleaning power + a pretty design. Highly recommended! [[[The 'Helpful' button makes me so excited]]]

Automatic door opening = a whole new world experience. When it's finished, the door pops open automatically to let the moisture escape and even air dry! Wow, this is a whole new world feature that only those who have used it truly understand. It's subtly stressful when you finish washing dishes but they aren't completely dry, but with this one, that worry is zero. There are higher-end models that even feature hot air drying, but I'm not so sure about that. The reason it's more convenient is that it's a 6-place setting. With the large 12-place setting, you have to wait for it to fill up, so it feels like you're dumping all the dishes in at once, but with the 6-place model, you can start it right after finishing a meal. For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. Since it's beige, it looks subtly luxurious in the kitchen. It's simple and not flashy, so it doesn't ruin the interior. It has that perfect "clean kitchen item" vibe. My husband even complimented it, saying the kitchen looks prettier now that we have this. Oh, right, and why is it so quiet? The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" But the Samsung dishwasher is so quiet that I find myself constantly checking to see if it's even working. Total summary of pros. Great cleaning power (no pre-washing needed). The automatic door opening and drying function is a game changer. Since it's a 6-place setting, it's great to run it right after every meal. The design is sleek and doesn't ruin the interior. There is a rinse aid dispenser, but it's useless to me since I use tablet detergent. Conclusion = Definitely a holy grail item. They say there are people who have never used a dishwasher, but there are no people who have only used one once. Yes, that is exactly me. Now that I'm freed from hand washing, my quality of life has truly improved. I can play with the kids or have a cup of coffee while it runs; for me, it's the best parenting and housekeeping item! Overall: A realistic size perfect for a mom + powerful cleaning power + a pretty design. Highly recommended! [[[The 'Helpful' button makes me so excited]]]

For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" When you add up the trays, spoons, chopsticks, and water cups, it is literally a dishwashing hell. I used to use a Cuckoo 3-place dishwasher, but it broke down, so I did the dishes by hand for a while—I actually shed a few tears back then. (The repair cost was about the same as buying a new one.) A large 12-place model was too much of a burden, so I was looking for just the right size for 6 and managed to snag it for the mid-400,000 won range thanks to a credit card discount! Cleaning power? No pre-washing, just cleanliness. I'm too lazy to pre-wash, so I usually just rinse them quickly with water and put them in. But this thing really cleaned everything so thoroughly that I was amazed. Even soup stains and rice residue vanished completely! You just put in the detergent tablets, and it takes care of everything automatically, so it feels like a smart housekeeping assistant. Automatic door opening = a whole new world experience. When it's finished, the door pops open automatically to let the moisture escape and even air dry! Wow, this is a whole new world feature that only those who have used it truly understand. It's subtly stressful when you finish washing dishes but they aren't completely dry, but with this one, that worry is zero. There are higher-end models that even feature hot air drying, but I'm not so sure about that. The reason it's more convenient is that it's a 6-place setting. With the large 12-place setting, you have to wait for it to fill up, so it feels like you're dumping all the dishes in at once, but with the 6-place model, you can start it right after finishing a meal. For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. Since it's beige, it looks subtly luxurious in the kitchen. It's simple and not flashy, so it doesn't ruin the interior. It has that perfect "clean kitchen item" vibe. My husband even complimented it, saying the kitchen looks prettier now that we have this. Oh, right, and why is it so quiet? The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" But the Samsung dishwasher is so quiet that I find myself constantly checking to see if it's even working. Total summary of pros. Great cleaning power (no pre-washing needed). The automatic door opening and drying function is a game changer. Since it's a 6-place setting, it's great to run it right after every meal. The design is sleek and doesn't ruin the interior. Honestly, there are some downsides. Large pots and pans still need to be hand-washed. (But we use a huge 30-inch frying pan, so it would probably be a bit awkward to fit that in a 12-place setting anyway.) The amount you can put in at once is limited compared to the 12-place setting. There is a rinse aid dispenser, but it's useless to me since I use tablet detergent. Conclusion = Definitely a holy grail item. They say there are people who have never used a dishwasher, but there are no people who have only used one once. Yes, that is exactly me. Now that I'm freed from hand washing, my quality of life has truly improved. I can play with the kids or have a cup of coffee while it runs; for me, it's the best parenting and housekeeping item! Overall: A realistic size perfect for a mom + powerful cleaning power + a pretty design. Highly recommended! [[[The 'Helpful' button makes me so excited]]]

Even soup stains and rice residue vanished completely! You just put in the detergent tablets, and it takes care of everything automatically, so it feels like a smart housekeeping assistant. Automatic door opening = a whole new world experience. When it's finished, the door pops open automatically to let the moisture escape and even air dry! Wow, this is a whole new world feature that only those who have used it truly understand. It's subtly stressful when you finish washing dishes but they aren't completely dry, but with this one, that worry is zero. There are higher-end models that even feature hot air drying, but I'm not so sure about that. The reason it's more convenient is that it's a 6-place setting. With the large 12-place setting, you have to wait for it to fill up, so it feels like you're dumping all the dishes in at once, but with the 6-place model, you can start it right after finishing a meal. For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. Since it's beige, it looks subtly luxurious in the kitchen. It's simple and not flashy, so it doesn't ruin the interior. It has that perfect "clean kitchen item" vibe. My husband even complimented it, saying the kitchen looks prettier now that we have this. Oh, right, and why is it so quiet? The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" But the Samsung dishwasher is so quiet that I find myself constantly checking to see if it's even working. Total summary of pros. Great cleaning power (no pre-washing needed). The automatic door opening and drying function is a game changer. Since it's a 6-place setting, it's great to run it right after every meal. The design is sleek and doesn't ruin the interior. Honestly, there are some downsides. Large pots and pans still need to be hand-washed. (But we use a huge 30-inch frying pan, so it would probably be a bit awkward to fit that in a 12-place setting anyway.) The amount you can put in at once is limited compared to the 12-place setting. There is a rinse aid dispenser, but it's useless to me since I use tablet detergent. Conclusion = Definitely a holy grail item. They say there are people who have never used a dishwasher, but there are no people who have only used one once. Yes, that is exactly me. Now that I'm freed from hand washing, my quality of life has truly improved. I can play with the kids or have a cup of coffee while it runs; for me, it's the best parenting and housekeeping item! Overall: A realistic size perfect for a mom + powerful cleaning power + a pretty design. Highly recommended! [[[The 'Helpful' button makes me so excited]]]

For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" Samsung 6-person dishwasher, you are my destiny. ] || ---------------- || With three kids, a single meal results in a mountain of dishes! When you add up the trays, spoons, chopsticks, and water cups, it is literally a dishwashing hell. I used to use a Cuckoo 3-place dishwasher, but it broke down, so I did the dishes by hand for a while—I actually shed a few tears back then. (The repair cost was about the same as buying a new one.) A large 12-place model was too much of a burden, so I was looking for just the right size for 6 and managed to snag it for the mid-400,000 won range thanks to a credit card discount! Cleaning power? No pre-washing, just cleanliness. I'm too lazy to pre-wash, so I usually just rinse them quickly with water and put them in. But this thing really cleaned everything so thoroughly that I was amazed. Even soup stains and rice residue vanished completely! You just put in the detergent tablets, and it takes care of everything automatically, so it feels like a smart housekeeping assistant. Automatic door opening = a whole new world experience. When it's finished, the door pops open automatically to let the moisture escape and even air dry! Wow, this is a whole new world feature that only those who have used it truly understand. It's subtly stressful when you finish washing dishes but they aren't completely dry, but with this one, that worry is zero. There are higher-end models that even feature hot air drying, but I'm not so sure about that. The reason it's more convenient is that it's a 6-place setting. With the large 12-place setting, you have to wait for it to fill up, so it feels like you're dumping all the dishes in at once, but with the 6-place model, you can start it right after finishing a meal. For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. Since it's beige, it looks subtly luxurious in the kitchen. It's simple and not flashy, so it doesn't ruin the interior. It has that perfect "clean kitchen item" vibe. My husband even complimented it, saying the kitchen looks prettier now that we have this. Oh, right, and why is it so quiet? The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" But the Samsung dishwasher is so quiet that I find myself constantly checking to see if it's even working. Total summary of pros. Great cleaning power (no pre-washing needed). The automatic door opening and drying function is a game changer. Since it's a 6-place setting, it's great to run it right after every meal. The design is sleek and doesn't ruin the interior. Honestly, there are some downsides. Large pots and pans still need to be hand-washed. (But we use a huge 30-inch frying pan, so it would probably be a bit awkward to fit that in a 12-place setting anyway.) The amount you can put in at once is limited compared to the 12-place setting. There is a rinse aid dispenser, but it's useless to me since I use tablet detergent. Conclusion = Definitely a holy grail item. They say there are people who have never used a dishwasher, but there are no people who have only used one once. Yes, that is exactly me. Now that I'm freed from hand washing, my quality of life has truly improved. I can play with the kids or have a cup of coffee while it runs; for me, it's the best parenting and housekeeping item! Overall: A realistic size perfect for a mom + powerful cleaning power + a pretty design. Highly recommended! [[[The 'Helpful' button makes me so excited]]]

Automatic door opening = a whole new world experience. When it's finished, the door pops open automatically to let the moisture escape and even air dry! Wow, this is a whole new world feature that only those who have used it truly understand. It's subtly stressful when you finish washing dishes but they aren't completely dry, but with this one, that worry is zero. There are higher-end models that even feature hot air drying, but I'm not so sure about that. The reason it's more convenient is that it's a 6-place setting. With the large 12-place setting, you have to wait for it to fill up, so it feels like you're dumping all the dishes in at once, but with the 6-place model, you can start it right after finishing a meal. For me, this is actually much more practical! Because I can just quickly wash large pots and pans by hand. The design gets a passing grade too. Since it's beige, it looks subtly luxurious in the kitchen. It's simple and not flashy, so it doesn't ruin the interior. It has that perfect "clean kitchen item" vibe. My husband even complimented it, saying the kitchen looks prettier now that we have this. Oh, right, and why is it so quiet? The dishwasher I used before used to go around telling everyone in the neighborhood, "I'm washing dishes! I'm drying now!" They say there are people who have never used a dishwasher, but there are no people who have only used one once. Yes, that is exactly me. Sentence (English): Why did I wait so long to buy a dishwasher?
Comments (English): [ Why did you only buy this now? ] || ---------------- || Why did I wait so long to buy a dishwasher? I regret buying it so late. Can things really be this convenient? Comments (English): [ Samsung dishwasher for 6 people, made with my own money ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to write a review~ I wanted to use it enough and write a proper review after using it~ -------------------------------------------------- 6/12 Purchase + Peace of Mind Care 5-year free warranty 6/13 Installation 7/21 Water leak, received at AS center 7/24 AS technician visited, new product exchange confirmed 7/31 Exchange completed -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to put away the dishes and saw that the bottom of the sink was soaked with water~ I thought it was strange, so I turned on the dishwasher and saw that water was dripping through the gap in the back, so I applied for AS that morning~ The fastest visit took 3 days~ Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician disassembled the entire body and checked the symptoms. He said that it was a case he had never seen before and that it would be difficult to replace parts. He said that if a problem occurs within a month of installation, it is possible to exchange it, but unfortunately, since it was already a month later, he said that he would contact the headquarters and see if an exchange was possible,,, and fortunately, the exchange decision was made, so I exchanged it for a new product and am still using it well~ (I wasn't lucky with the draw, but I got an exchange, so Thank goodness) I went back to the dishwashing hell for 10 days and ate out a lot -------------------------------------------------------------- I've been married for 8 years, but since both of us work, we didn't cook much at home, so we lived without a dishwasher. After the baby was born, I had to prepare the baby's food regularly, so the amount of dishes increased, and I thought I really needed to buy one. I thought that if I continued like this, my relationship with my husband would become more distant, so I held out and bought it~ I was worried until the day of payment. I had doubts like, "Is this really your aunt?" and I thought that it would need a lot of water since it runs for over an hour, so I think I delayed the purchase a bit more because of my worries about the management fee. I bought it for around 400,000 won with a card discount and also registered for the peace of mind care. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!) and two technicians came, and unlike other reviews, they were very friendly. It was possible to extend the pipe through the gap without drilling holes like a water purifier, but I drilled holes because they said that the water pressure might drop and I might need to reinstall it. Drilling took less than 30 seconds. There is no manual, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I chose standard, rapid, and powerful? I've only been using that function, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the ProgMini that everyone uses, and I used the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It took a while because I'm not good at Tetris, but now it's very fast after doing it every day. I hate the smell caused by food scraps and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in. (I just skim out the food, leaving the grease in.) Maybe that's why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there's no smell at all. Except for large pots, it can easily hold enough dishes for a meal for a family of three, and the operating noise is almost the same as the noise from everyday life. (It doesn't bother me at all when I have the TV on in the living room or playing with the baby.) A few minutes before the dishwasher is finished, the lid opens, letting the hot steam escape. If it's left that way, even after a day, moisture remains, so to increase the natural drying effect, I open the door wide before going to bed, take the drying rack outside, and put the dishes away the next morning. (I use smooth dishes or The cups are all dry, but there is still moisture in the grooves and curved parts like the lid of the lunch box, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish~) Using the dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar. But as I quickly got used to it, I thought, "This is why they call it 'auntie, aunt'" and while I resented myself for buying it late, I praised myself for making a good purchase ^^ I'll summarize what I've felt for nearly three months~ Pros: The stress of washing dishes has disappeared (I used to multi-task while washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden, and I just run the dishwasher at the end and that's it!) My legs don't hurt because the dishwashing time has been shortened, and the baby waits for me less and plays with the baby more (I'm so happy). My husband and I don't fight anymore, and he doesn't hate me, and his stress has also decreased. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. I don't know if it's a problem with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, but white water stains (residual detergent?) can be seen in small crevices (the same thing happens even if I split the detergent or add an extra rinse. ) So there is the hassle of double washing (I often rinse baby dishes with hot water again out of concern) After the operation is over and you leave it as is, the water does not dry at all Overall: I didn't feel much of a change in the management cost (electricity bill, water bill) that I was worried about before and after the dishwasher was installed~ (I didn't check the exact unit ^^;) It would be more convenient if there was hot air drying, but it's not that difficult for me to open the door and take out the drying rack before going to bed~ The kitchen space has gotten smaller, but it's actually easier to organize and the kitchen has become neater~ The hassle of rinsing the white part (I suspect detergent residue) that is visible in the gap between the baby's plates is bearable~ It could be a detergent problem, so I'm going to try changing it once in the middle~ I think I know why people around me recommend a dishwasher~ I'm 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take long for others. Comments (English): [ Samsung dishwasher for 6 people, made with my own money ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to write a review~ I wanted to use it enough and write a proper review after using it~ -------------------------------------------------- 6/12 Purchase + Peace of Mind Care 5-year free warranty 6/13 Installation 7/21 Water leak, received at AS center 7/24 AS technician visited, new product exchange confirmed 7/31 Exchange completed -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to put away the dishes and saw that the bottom of the sink was soaked with water~ I thought it was strange, so I turned on the dishwasher and saw that water was dripping through the gap in the back, so I applied for AS that morning~ The fastest visit took 3 days~ Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician disassembled the entire body and checked the symptoms. After the baby was born, I had to prepare the baby's food regularly, so the amount of dishes increased, and I thought I really needed to buy one. I thought that if I continued like this, my relationship with my husband would become more distant, so I held out and bought it~ I was worried until the day of payment. I had doubts like, "Is this really your aunt?" and I thought that it would need a lot of water since it runs for over an hour, so I think I delayed the purchase a bit more because of my worries about the management fee. I bought it for around 400,000 won with a card discount and also registered for the peace of mind care. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!) and two technicians came, and unlike other reviews, they were very friendly. It was possible to extend the pipe through the gap without drilling holes like a water purifier, but I drilled holes because they said that the water pressure might drop and I might need to reinstall it. Drilling took less than 30 seconds. There is no manual, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I chose standard, rapid, and powerful? I've only been using that function, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the ProgMini that everyone uses, and I used the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It took a while because I'm not good at Tetris, but now it's very fast after doing it every day. I hate the smell caused by food scraps and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in. (I just skim out the food, leaving the grease in.) Maybe that's why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there's no smell at all. Except for large pots, it can easily hold enough dishes for a meal for a family of three, and the operating noise is almost the same as the noise from everyday life. (It doesn't bother me at all when I have the TV on in the living room or playing with the baby.) A few minutes before the dishwasher is finished, the lid opens, letting the hot steam escape. If it's left that way, even after a day, moisture remains, so to increase the natural drying effect, I open the door wide before going to bed, take the drying rack outside, and put the dishes away the next morning. (I use smooth dishes or The cups are all dry, but there is still moisture in the grooves and curved parts like the lid of the lunch box, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish~) Using the dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar. But as I quickly got used to it, I thought, "This is why they call it 'auntie, aunt'" and while I resented myself for buying it late, I praised myself for making a good purchase ^^ I'll summarize what I've felt for nearly three months~ Pros: The stress of washing dishes has disappeared (I used to multi-task while washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden, and I just run the dishwasher at the end and that's it!) My legs don't hurt because the dishwashing time has been shortened, and the baby waits for me less and plays with the baby more (I'm so happy). My husband and I don't fight anymore, and he doesn't hate me, and his stress has also decreased. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. I don't know if it's a problem with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, but white water stains (residual detergent?) can be seen in small crevices (the same thing happens even if I split the detergent or add an extra rinse. ) So there is the hassle of double washing (I often rinse baby dishes with hot water again out of concern) After the operation is over and you leave it as is, the water does not dry at all Overall: I didn't feel much of a change in the management cost (electricity bill, water bill) that I was worried about before and after the dishwasher was installed~ (I didn't check the exact unit ^^;) It would be more convenient if there was hot air drying, but it's not that difficult for me to open the door and take out the drying rack before going to bed~ The kitchen space has gotten smaller, but it's actually easier to organize and the kitchen has become neater~ The hassle of rinsing the white part (I suspect detergent residue) that is visible in the gap between the baby's plates is bearable~ It could be a detergent problem, so I'm going to try changing it once in the middle~ I think I know why people around me recommend a dishwasher~ I'm 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take long for others. It's time to welcome my aunt. ^^ Since purchasing the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought over the dishes once! It's brought peace to our family, and it's no exaggeration to say it's the smartest purchase I made this year! Above all, it's a truly precious product that has given me precious evening time with my baby. This is my honest review after using it for three months, so I hope it's helpful to those of you who are currently considering it. ^^

ㅠㅠ) 같은게 보인다 (세제를 쪼개도, 헹굼 추가해도 마찬가지예요...) 그래서 이중으로 세척하는 번거로움이 있다 ㅠㅠ (아기식기는 걱정되어 뜨거운 물로 한번 더 문질러서 헹굴때가 종종 있어요 ㅠㅠ) 작동이 끝나고 그대로 두면 물이 전혀 마르지 않는다  총평 : 우려했던 관리비 (전기세, 물세)는 식세기 전과 후에 큰 변화를 느끼지 못했어요~ (원단위까지 꼼꼼하게 따져보진 않았습니다 ^^;)  열풍건조가 되면 더 편하겠지만 자기전에 문열고 건조대 빼는게 저에게는 크게 힘들지 않아요~ 주방 사용공간은 좁아졌지만 오히려 정리정돈이 수월해지면서 주방이 깔끔해졌어요~  아기식판틈에 보이는 하얀부분(잔류세제 의심)은 추가로 헹궈주는 번거로움은 견딜만 해요~ 세제 문제일수도 있으니 중간에 한번 바꿔보도록 하려구요~ 왜 주변에서 식세기를 추천하는지 알것같아요~  저는 8년이나 늦었지만 다른분들은 오래 안걸리셨으면 좋겠네요 이모님 맞이하는 시간이요..^^  식세기 구매 후에는 남편이랑 설거지 때문에 싸운적이 한번도 없어요~ 가족의 평화를 주었고 올해 가장 현명한 소비품이라고 해도 과언이 아니예요!! 무엇보다도 저녁에 아기와 보내는 소중한 시간을 선물해준 정말 고마운 제품이랍니다~ 3개월간 사용하면서 느낀 솔직한 리뷰이니 현재 고민하시는 분들에게 도움이 되셨음 좋겠어요 ^^

Comments (English): [ Samsung dishwasher for 6 people, made with my own money ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to write a review~ I wanted to use it enough and write a proper review after using it~ -------------------------------------------------- 6/12 Purchase + Peace of Mind Care 5-year free warranty 6/13 Installation 7/21 Water leak, received at AS center 7/24 AS technician visited, new product exchange confirmed 7/31 Exchange completed -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to put away the dishes and saw that the bottom of the sink was soaked with water~ I thought it was strange, so I turned on the dishwasher and saw that water was dripping through the gap in the back, so I applied for AS that morning~ The fastest visit took 3 days~ Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician disassembled the entire body and checked the symptoms. He said that it was a case he had never seen before and that it would be difficult to replace parts. He said that if a problem occurs within a month of installation, it is possible to exchange it, but unfortunately, since it was already a month later, he said that he would contact the headquarters and see if an exchange was possible,,, and fortunately, the exchange decision was made, so I exchanged it for a new product and am still using it well~ (I wasn't lucky with the draw, but I got an exchange, so Thank goodness) I went back to the dishwashing hell for 10 days and ate out a lot -------------------------------------------------------------- I've been married for 8 years, but since both of us work, we didn't cook much at home, so we lived without a dishwasher. After the baby was born, I had to prepare the baby's food regularly, so the amount of dishes increased, and I thought I really needed to buy one. I thought that if I continued like this, my relationship with my husband would become more distant, so I held out and bought it~ I was worried until the day of payment. I had doubts like, "Is this really your aunt?" and I thought that it would need a lot of water since it runs for over an hour, so I think I delayed the purchase a bit more because of my worries about the management fee. I bought it for around 400,000 won with a card discount and also registered for the peace of mind care. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!) and two technicians came, and unlike other reviews, they were very friendly. It was possible to extend the pipe through the gap without drilling holes like a water purifier, but I drilled holes because they said that the water pressure might drop and I might need to reinstall it. Drilling took less than 30 seconds. There is no manual, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I chose standard, rapid, and powerful? I've only been using that function, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the ProgMini that everyone uses, and I used the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It took a while because I'm not good at Tetris, but now it's very fast after doing it every day. I hate the smell caused by food scraps and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in. (I just skim out the food, leaving the grease in.) Maybe that's why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there's no smell at all. Except for large pots, it can easily hold enough dishes for a meal for a family of three, and the operating noise is almost the same as the noise from everyday life. (It doesn't bother me at all when I have the TV on in the living room or playing with the baby.) A few minutes before the dishwasher is finished, the lid opens, letting the hot steam escape. If it's left that way, even after a day, moisture remains, so to increase the natural drying effect, I open the door wide before going to bed, take the drying rack outside, and put the dishes away the next morning. (I use smooth dishes or The cups are all dry, but there is still moisture in the grooves and curved parts like the lid of the lunch box, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish~) Using the dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar. But as I quickly got used to it, I thought, "This is why they call it 'auntie, aunt'" and while I resented myself for buying it late, I praised myself for making a good purchase ^^ I'll summarize what I've felt for nearly three months~ Pros: The stress of washing dishes has disappeared (I used to multi-task while washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden, and I just run the dishwasher at the end and that's it!) My legs don't hurt because the dishwashing time has been shortened, and the baby waits for me less and plays with the baby more (I'm so happy). My husband and I don't fight anymore, and he doesn't hate me, and his stress has also decreased. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. I don't know if it's a problem with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, but white water stains (residual detergent?) can be seen in small crevices (the same thing happens even if I split the detergent or add an extra rinse. ) So there is the hassle of double washing (I often rinse baby dishes with hot water again out of concern) After the operation is over and you leave it as is, the water does not dry at all Overall: I didn't feel much of a change in the management cost (electricity bill, water bill) that I was worried about before and after the dishwasher was installed~ (I didn't check the exact unit ^^;) It would be more convenient if there was hot air drying, but it's not that difficult for me to open the door and take out the drying rack before going to bed~ The kitchen space has gotten smaller, but it's actually easier to organize and the kitchen has become neater~ The hassle of rinsing the white part (I suspect detergent residue) that is visible in the gap between the baby's plates is bearable~ It could be a detergent problem, so I'm going to try changing it once in the middle~ I think I know why people around me recommend a dishwasher~ I'm 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take long for others. It's time to welcome my aunt. ^^ Since purchasing the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought over the dishes once! It's brought peace to our family, and it's no exaggeration to say it's the smartest purchase I made this year! Above all, it's a truly precious product that has given me precious evening time with my baby. This is my honest review after using it for three months, so I hope it's helpful to those of you who are currently considering it. ^^

ㅠㅠ) 같은게 보인다 (세제를 쪼개도, 헹굼 추가해도 마찬가지예요...) 그래서 이중으로 세척하는 번거로움이 있다 ㅠㅠ (아기식기는 걱정되어 뜨거운 물로 한번 더 문질러서 헹굴때가 종종 있어요 ㅠㅠ) 작동이 끝나고 그대로 두면 물이 전혀 마르지 않는다  총평 : 우려했던 관리비 (전기세, 물세)는 식세기 전과 후에 큰 변화를 느끼지 못했어요~ (원단위까지 꼼꼼하게 따져보진 않았습니다 ^^;)  열풍건조가 되면 더 편하겠지만 자기전에 문열고 건조대 빼는게 저에게는 크게 힘들지 않아요~ 주방 사용공간은 좁아졌지만 오히려 정리정돈이 수월해지면서 주방이 깔끔해졌어요~  아기식판틈에 보이는 하얀부분(잔류세제 의심)은 추가로 헹궈주는 번거로움은 견딜만 해요~ 세제 문제일수도 있으니 중간에 한번 바꿔보도록 하려구요~ 왜 주변에서 식세기를 추천하는지 알것같아요~  저는 8년이나 늦었지만 다른분들은 오래 안걸리셨으면 좋겠네요 이모님 맞이하는 시간이요..^^  식세기 구매 후에는 남편이랑 설거지 때문에 싸운적이 한번도 없어요~ 가족의 평화를 주었고 올해 가장 현명한 소비품이라고 해도 과언이 아니예요!! 무엇보다도 저녁에 아기와 보내는 소중한 시간을 선물해준 정말 고마운 제품이랍니다~ 3개월간 사용하면서 느낀 솔직한 리뷰이니 현재 고민하시는 분들에게 도움이 되셨음 좋겠어요 ^^

Comments (English): [ Samsung dishwasher for 6 people, made with my own money ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to write a review~ I wanted to use it enough and write a proper review after using it~ -------------------------------------------------- 6/12 Purchase + Peace of Mind Care 5-year free warranty 6/13 Installation 7/21 Water leak, received at AS center 7/24 AS technician visited, new product exchange confirmed 7/31 Exchange completed -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to put away the dishes and saw that the bottom of the sink was soaked with water~ I thought it was strange, so I turned on the dishwasher and saw that water was dripping through the gap in the back, so I applied for AS that morning~ The fastest visit took 3 days~ Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician disassembled the entire body and checked the symptoms. He said that it was a case he had never seen before and that it would be difficult to replace parts. He said that if a problem occurs within a month of installation, it is possible to exchange it, but unfortunately, since it was already a month later, he said that he would contact the headquarters and see if an exchange was possible,,, and fortunately, the exchange decision was made, so I exchanged it for a new product and am still using it well~ (I wasn't lucky with the draw, but I got an exchange, so Thank goodness) I went back to the dishwashing hell for 10 days and ate out a lot -------------------------------------------------------------- I've been married for 8 years, but since both of us work, we didn't cook much at home, so we lived without a dishwasher. After the baby was born, I had to prepare the baby's food regularly, so the amount of dishes increased, and I thought I really needed to buy one. I thought that if I continued like this, my relationship with my husband would become more distant, so I held out and bought it~ I was worried until the day of payment. I had doubts like, "Is this really your aunt?" and I thought that it would need a lot of water since it runs for over an hour, so I think I delayed the purchase a bit more because of my worries about the management fee. I bought it for around 400,000 won with a card discount and also registered for the peace of mind care. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!) and two technicians came, and unlike other reviews, they were very friendly. It was possible to extend the pipe through the gap without drilling holes like a water purifier, but I drilled holes because they said that the water pressure might drop and I might need to reinstall it. Drilling took less than 30 seconds. There is no manual, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I chose standard, rapid, and powerful? I've only been using that function, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the ProgMini that everyone uses, and I used the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It took a while because I'm not good at Tetris, but now it's very fast after doing it every day. I hate the smell caused by food scraps and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in. (I just skim out the food, leaving the grease in.) Maybe that's why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there's no smell at all. Except for large pots, it can easily hold enough dishes for a meal for a family of three, and the operating noise is almost the same as the noise from everyday life. (It doesn't bother me at all when I have the TV on in the living room or playing with the baby.) A few minutes before the dishwasher is finished, the lid opens, letting the hot steam escape. If it's left that way, even after a day, moisture remains, so to increase the natural drying effect, I open the door wide before going to bed, take the drying rack outside, and put the dishes away the next morning. (I use smooth dishes or The cups are all dry, but there is still moisture in the grooves and curved parts like the lid of the lunch box, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish~) Using the dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar. But as I quickly got used to it, I thought, "This is why they call it 'auntie, aunt'" and while I resented myself for buying it late, I praised myself for making a good purchase ^^ I'll summarize what I've felt for nearly three months~ Pros: The stress of washing dishes has disappeared (I used to multi-task while washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden, and I just run the dishwasher at the end and that's it!) My legs don't hurt because the dishwashing time has been shortened, and the baby waits for me less and plays with the baby more (I'm so happy). My husband and I don't fight anymore, and he doesn't hate me, and his stress has also decreased. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. I don't know if it's a problem with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, but white water stains (residual detergent?) can be seen in small crevices (the same thing happens even if I split the detergent or add an extra rinse. ) So there is the hassle of double washing (I often rinse baby dishes with hot water again out of concern) After the operation is over and you leave it as is, the water does not dry at all Overall: I didn't feel much of a change in the management cost (electricity bill, water bill) that I was worried about before and after the dishwasher was installed~ (I didn't check the exact unit ^^;) It would be more convenient if there was hot air drying, but it's not that difficult for me to open the door and take out the drying rack before going to bed~ The kitchen space has gotten smaller, but it's actually easier to organize and the kitchen has become neater~ The hassle of rinsing the white part (I suspect detergent residue) that is visible in the gap between the baby's plates is bearable~ It could be a detergent problem, so I'm going to try changing it once in the middle~ I think I know why people around me recommend a dishwasher~ I'm 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take long for others. It's time to welcome my aunt. ^^ Since purchasing the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought over the dishes once! It's brought peace to our family, and it's no exaggeration to say it's the smartest purchase I made this year! Above all, it's a truly precious product that has given me precious evening time with my baby. This is my honest review after using it for three months, so I hope it's helpful to those of you who are currently considering it. ^^

그 기능만 돌려쓰고 있어서 아직 크게 어려운점은 없네요~  식세기 도착 전 다들 쓰신다는 프로그미니를 준비해 놓고 설치당일 저녁에 식세기를 처음 돌려 보았어요~ 테트리스가 서툴러 시간이 좀 걸렸는데 매일 하다보니 이제는 속도가 굉장히 빠르답니다~~ 저는 음식찌꺼기로 인해 발생되는 냄새와 잦은 거름망 청소가 싫어서 찬물로 애벌설거지를 한번 하고 넣어요~ (음식물만 걷어내는 정도, 기름기는 그대로 둠) 그래서인지 아직 거름망청소 알람이 울린적은 없어요 냄새도 전혀 안나고요~ 커다란 냄비류 빼고는 요리포함 3인식구 한끼식사 식기류를 거뜬히 들어가고 작동 소리는 생활소음과 거의 맞먹어요~ (거실에 티비를 틀어놓거나 아기랑 놀때 전혀 신경쓰이지 않아요) 식세기 끝나기 몇분 전 뚜껑이 열리면서 뜨거운 김이 빠지고 그 상태로는 하루가 지나도 물기가 그대로 남아 있기 때문에 자연건조 효과를 높이기 위해 자기 전 문을 활짝 열어서 건조대를 바깥으로 빼주고 다음날 아침에 식기를 정리합니다~ (매끈한 그릇이나 컵은 다 말라있지만 그래도 반찬통 뚜껑같은 홈이나 굴곡진 부분에는 물기가 남아있어 키친타올로 닦아서 마무리해요~)  첫 식세기 사용이 다소 낯설었지만... 금방 적응이 되면서 \'이래서 이모님이모님 하는구나 ㅠㅠ\' 라는 생각에 늦게 구매한 저를 원망하면서도 이제라도 잘샀다 하고 스스로를 칭찬했어요 ^^ 세달가까이 느낀점을 정리해보겠습니다~  장점 : 설거지 스트레스가 사라졌다 (요리할때 설거지하면서 멀티로 했는데 이제는 요리만 하면서 식기를 많이 사용해도 부담 없고 마지막에 식세기 돌려주면 끝!!) 설거지 시간이 단축되면서 다리가 안아프다, 아기가 엄마를 기다려주는 시간이 줄었고 아기랑 놀아주는 시간이 늘어났다 (너무 행복해요 ㅠㅠ)  남편이랑 안싸운다, 남편이 안밉다, 남편도 스트레스가 줄었다고 한다....!!!!  단점 : 주방이 좁아졌다 ㅠㅠ 세제의 문제인지 식세기 세정력에 문제인지 작은 틈 사이에 하얀물때 (잔류세제? ㅠㅠ) 같은게 보인다 (세제를 쪼개도, 헹굼 추가해도 마찬가지예요...) 그래서 이중으로 세척하는 번거로움이 있다 ㅠㅠ (아기식기는 걱정되어 뜨거운 물로 한번 더 문질러서 헹굴때가 종종 있어요 ㅠㅠ) 작동이 끝나고 그대로 두면 물이 전혀 마르지 않는다  총평 : 우려했던 관리비 (전기세, 물세)는 식세기 전과 후에 큰 변화를 느끼지 못했어요~ (원단위까지 꼼꼼하게 따져보진 않았습니다 ^^;)  열풍건조가 되면 더 편하겠지만 자기전에 문열고 건조대 빼는게 저에게는 크게 힘들지 않아요~ 주방 사용공간은 좁아졌지만 오히려 정리정돈이 수월해지면서 주방이 깔끔해졌어요~  아기식판틈에 보이는 하얀부분(잔류세제 의심)은 추가로 헹궈주는 번거로움은 견딜만 해요~ 세제 문제일수도 있으니 중간에 한번 바꿔보도록 하려구요~ 왜 주변에서 식세기를 추천하는지 알것같아요~  저는 8년이나 늦었지만 다른분들은 오래 안걸리셨으면 좋겠네요 이모님 맞이하는 시간이요..^^  식세기 구매 후에는 남편이랑 설거지 때문에 싸운적이 한번도 없어요~ 가족의 평화를 주었고 올해 가장 현명한 소비품이라고 해도 과언이 아니예요!! 무엇보다도 저녁에 아기와 보내는 소중한 시간을 선물해준 정말 고마운 제품이랍니다~ 3개월간 사용하면서 느낀 솔직한 리뷰이니 현재 고민하시는 분들에게 도움이 되셨음 좋겠어요 ^^

Comments (English): [ Samsung dishwasher for 6 people, made with my own money ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to write a review~ I wanted to use it enough and write a proper review after using it~ -------------------------------------------------- 6/12 Purchase + Peace of Mind Care 5-year free warranty 6/13 Installation 7/21 Water leak, received at AS center 7/24 AS technician visited, new product exchange confirmed 7/31 Exchange completed -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to put away the dishes and saw that the bottom of the sink was soaked with water~ I thought it was strange, so I turned on the dishwasher and saw that water was dripping through the gap in the back, so I applied for AS that morning~ The fastest visit took 3 days~ Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician disassembled the entire body and checked the symptoms. He said that it was a case he had never seen before and that it would be difficult to replace parts. He said that if a problem occurs within a month of installation, it is possible to exchange it, but unfortunately, since it was already a month later, he said that he would contact the headquarters and see if an exchange was possible,,, and fortunately, the exchange decision was made, so I exchanged it for a new product and am still using it well~ (I wasn't lucky with the draw, but I got an exchange, so Thank goodness) I went back to the dishwashing hell for 10 days and ate out a lot -------------------------------------------------------------- I've been married for 8 years, but since both of us work, we didn't cook much at home, so we lived without a dishwasher. After the baby was born, I had to prepare the baby's food regularly, so the amount of dishes increased, and I thought I really needed to buy one. I thought that if I continued like this, my relationship with my husband would become more distant, so I held out and bought it~ I was worried until the day of payment. I had doubts like, "Is this really your aunt?" and I thought that it would need a lot of water since it runs for over an hour, so I think I delayed the purchase a bit more because of my worries about the management fee. I bought it for around 400,000 won with a card discount and also registered for the peace of mind care. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!) and two technicians came, and unlike other reviews, they were very friendly. It was possible to extend the pipe through the gap without drilling holes like a water purifier, but I drilled holes because they said that the water pressure might drop and I might need to reinstall it. Drilling took less than 30 seconds. There is no manual, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I chose standard, rapid, and powerful? I've only been using that function, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the ProgMini that everyone uses, and I used the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It took a while because I'm not good at Tetris, but now it's very fast after doing it every day. I hate the smell caused by food scraps and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in. (I just skim out the food, leaving the grease in.) Maybe that's why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there's no smell at all. Except for large pots, it can easily hold enough dishes for a meal for a family of three, and the operating noise is almost the same as the noise from everyday life. (It doesn't bother me at all when I have the TV on in the living room or playing with the baby.) A few minutes before the dishwasher is finished, the lid opens, letting the hot steam escape. If it's left that way, even after a day, moisture remains, so to increase the natural drying effect, I open the door wide before going to bed, take the drying rack outside, and put the dishes away the next morning. (I use smooth dishes or The cups are all dry, but there is still moisture in the grooves and curved parts like the lid of the lunch box, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish~) Using the dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar. But as I quickly got used to it, I thought, "This is why they call it 'auntie, aunt'" and while I resented myself for buying it late, I praised myself for making a good purchase ^^ I'll summarize what I've felt for nearly three months~ Pros: The stress of washing dishes has disappeared (I used to multi-task while washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden, and I just run the dishwasher at the end and that's it!) My legs don't hurt because the dishwashing time has been shortened, and the baby waits for me less and plays with the baby more (I'm so happy). My husband and I don't fight anymore, and he doesn't hate me, and his stress has also decreased. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. I don't know if it's a problem with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, but white water stains (residual detergent?) can be seen in small crevices (the same thing happens even if I split the detergent or add an extra rinse. ) So there is the hassle of double washing (I often rinse baby dishes with hot water again out of concern) After the operation is over and you leave it as is, the water does not dry at all Overall: I didn't feel much of a change in the management cost (electricity bill, water bill) that I was worried about before and after the dishwasher was installed~ (I didn't check the exact unit ^^;) It would be more convenient if there was hot air drying, but it's not that difficult for me to open the door and take out the drying rack before going to bed~ The kitchen space has gotten smaller, but it's actually easier to organize and the kitchen has become neater~ The hassle of rinsing the white part (I suspect detergent residue) that is visible in the gap between the baby's plates is bearable~ It could be a detergent problem, so I'm going to try changing it once in the middle~ I think I know why people around me recommend a dishwasher~ I'm 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take long for others. It's time to welcome my aunt. ^^ Since purchasing the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought over the dishes once! It's brought peace to our family, and it's no exaggeration to say it's the smartest purchase I made this year! Above all, it's a truly precious product that has given me precious evening time with my baby. This is my honest review after using it for three months, so I hope it's helpful to those of you who are currently considering it. ^^

그 기능만 돌려쓰고 있어서 아직 크게 어려운점은 없네요~  식세기 도착 전 다들 쓰신다는 프로그미니를 준비해 놓고 설치당일 저녁에 식세기를 처음 돌려 보았어요~ 테트리스가 서툴러 시간이 좀 걸렸는데 매일 하다보니 이제는 속도가 굉장히 빠르답니다~~ 저는 음식찌꺼기로 인해 발생되는 냄새와 잦은 거름망 청소가 싫어서 찬물로 애벌설거지를 한번 하고 넣어요~ (음식물만 걷어내는 정도, 기름기는 그대로 둠) 그래서인지 아직 거름망청소 알람이 울린적은 없어요 냄새도 전혀 안나고요~ 커다란 냄비류 빼고는 요리포함 3인식구 한끼식사 식기류를 거뜬히 들어가고 작동 소리는 생활소음과 거의 맞먹어요~ (거실에 티비를 틀어놓거나 아기랑 놀때 전혀 신경쓰이지 않아요) 식세기 끝나기 몇분 전 뚜껑이 열리면서 뜨거운 김이 빠지고 그 상태로는 하루가 지나도 물기가 그대로 남아 있기 때문에 자연건조 효과를 높이기 위해 자기 전 문을 활짝 열어서 건조대를 바깥으로 빼주고 다음날 아침에 식기를 정리합니다~ (매끈한 그릇이나 컵은 다 말라있지만 그래도 반찬통 뚜껑같은 홈이나 굴곡진 부분에는 물기가 남아있어 키친타올로 닦아서 마무리해요~)  첫 식세기 사용이 다소 낯설었지만... 금방 적응이 되면서 \'이래서 이모님이모님 하는구나 ㅠㅠ\' 라는 생각에 늦게 구매한 저를 원망하면서도 이제라도 잘샀다 하고 스스로를 칭찬했어요 ^^ 세달가까이 느낀점을 정리해보겠습니다~  장점 : 설거지 스트레스가 사라졌다 (요리할때 설거지하면서 멀티로 했는데 이제는 요리만 하면서 식기를 많이 사용해도 부담 없고 마지막에 식세기 돌려주면 끝!!) 설거지 시간이 단축되면서 다리가 안아프다, 아기가 엄마를 기다려주는 시간이 줄었고 아기랑 놀아주는 시간이 늘어났다 (너무 행복해요 ㅠㅠ)  남편이랑 안싸운다, 남편이 안밉다, 남편도 스트레스가 줄었다고 한다....!!!!  단점 : 주방이 좁아졌다 ㅠㅠ 세제의 문제인지 식세기 세정력에 문제인지 작은 틈 사이에 하얀물때 (잔류세제? ㅠㅠ) 같은게 보인다 (세제를 쪼개도, 헹굼 추가해도 마찬가지예요...) 그래서 이중으로 세척하는 번거로움이 있다 ㅠㅠ (아기식기는 걱정되어 뜨거운 물로 한번 더 문질러서 헹굴때가 종종 있어요 ㅠㅠ) 작동이 끝나고 그대로 두면 물이 전혀 마르지 않는다  총평 : 우려했던 관리비 (전기세, 물세)는 식세기 전과 후에 큰 변화를 느끼지 못했어요~ (원단위까지 꼼꼼하게 따져보진 않았습니다 ^^;)  열풍건조가 되면 더 편하겠지만 자기전에 문열고 건조대 빼는게 저에게는 크게 힘들지 않아요~ 주방 사용공간은 좁아졌지만 오히려 정리정돈이 수월해지면서 주방이 깔끔해졌어요~  아기식판틈에 보이는 하얀부분(잔류세제 의심)은 추가로 헹궈주는 번거로움은 견딜만 해요~ 세제 문제일수도 있으니 중간에 한번 바꿔보도록 하려구요~ 왜 주변에서 식세기를 추천하는지 알것같아요~  저는 8년이나 늦었지만 다른분들은 오래 안걸리셨으면 좋겠네요 이모님 맞이하는 시간이요..^^  식세기 구매 후에는 남편이랑 설거지 때문에 싸운적이 한번도 없어요~ 가족의 평화를 주었고 올해 가장 현명한 소비품이라고 해도 과언이 아니예요!! 무엇보다도 저녁에 아기와 보내는 소중한 시간을 선물해준 정말 고마운 제품이랍니다~ 3개월간 사용하면서 느낀 솔직한 리뷰이니 현재 고민하시는 분들에게 도움이 되셨음 좋겠어요 ^^
