Free yourself from the dishwashing! ] || ---------------- || This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Team event. Why I Purchased It: I live alone in a 1.5-room studio apartment, and I enjoy cooking! But the biggest challenge is washing dishes after meals. I always have to do them after every meal, but even though it's only a small amount, I sometimes feel like I shouldn't do it all at once, and it just gets tiresome. Lately, the hot summer has made my rubber gloves sweaty, and my hands get wet all the time, so I've even developed housewife eczema, which has been a major concern. Then, when I saw the Minix Mini dishwasher listed on the Coupang Experience Team, I immediately applied! Through this experience, I'll be testing it out to see if it's suitable for use in a studio apartment and if it's suitable for people living alone. ^^ Product Introduction, Features, and Components: The Minix Mini Dishwasher (MNDW-110CG) is designed for easy installation and convenient use. It has a compact size, powerful cleaning power, and various functions :) Size: 42cm wide, 44cm long, and 43.5cm high, it is compact and can fit even in small spaces. I thought it would be good to put it near the sink considering the drain pipe use. (I temporarily put it on the microwave shelf because there was no space. I'll think about where to put it later.) Washing function: There are three modes: Strong (55 minutes), Standard (40 minutes), and Rapid (25 minutes), so you can choose depending on the degree of contamination. Additionally, the hot water (high-temperature sterilization) function sterilizes 99.9% of harmful bacteria, so you can use it hygienically and safely! Contents: Main unit, dish basket, cutlery holder, water tank, water cup, drain hose, suction cup, etc. When the product arrived, it was safely packaged in a box, and various accessories were wrapped in plastic inside the main unit^^ Good point: Just the right size for a single room The best thing was probably the just the right size. Despite my small studio kitchen, I thought it would be a great space-saving solution because of its compact size. (Of course, I haven't thought about where to put it yet!) Perfect for 1-2 people. The product description says it's for 3 people, but when I first opened the unit and actually used it, I realized it was perfectly suited for 1-2 people. Specifically, I felt it would be enough to handle a day's worth of dishes for one person at a time. Intuitive design and ease of use: One of the most important aspects of this product for me is its intuitive design and ease of use. Thanks to this design, there's no complicated installation process; just plug it in, fill the water tank, and press the desired mode. It's incredibly convenient. Thanks to its intuitive design, I didn't even have to read the included manual. Furthermore, it's a no-drill installation (water pipe installation is optional), so I can just install the drain pipe and start using it right away, without having to scratch or remodel my studio! Disappointing Points: Only small dishes and cutlery can be washed. While this dishwasher is compact enough for one or two people, it unfortunately won't fit bulky items like frying pans or pots. This means you'll have to wash these bulky items yourself. If you want to wash bulky items, we recommend purchasing a larger version than the Minix! (The Minix dishwasher only supports glass and ceramic containers (including mugs), stainless steel containers, and cutlery sets.) Burden of Installation: While the intuitive design makes it easy to use, I felt the installation process could be a bit tedious. While using it by filling the tank with water eliminates the need for a water supply line, you'll need to install a drain hose, so be sure to carefully consider where to place the dishwasher. If it's not near the sink, drainage can be difficult. Limitations in narrow spaces In the 1.5 room detached space where I live, it was okay because I had space to put the dishwasher, but I thought that if I used it in an open-plan studio apartment of about 5-6 pyeong, it might feel stuffy because it would take up a lot of space. (If I'm not careful, I might end up looking like I'm buried in things in the house.) Also, I need to consider the space for the power cord and drain pipe, so I need to check the kitchen layout in advance. If I'm not careful, the dishwasher might take up the space I really need. Overall review of the product The Minix Mini Dishwasher is a product that I highly recommend to single-person households who hate doing dishes! With its compact size, ample capacity, and ease of use, it's a must-have for those living alone. Adding the hot air function dries them almost completely, so it’s great that I can put everything away right away. Since I don't cook often, I wondered if I would find it useful. But washing my baby's bottles, teething toys, baby food utensils, and everything else in it is so convenient. When I was raising my first child, I used a steam sterilizer and bought all sorts of baby appliances, which made the kitchen very messy. But with this dishwasher handling dishwashing, steam, and hot air all at once, the housework has been drastically reduced. Sentence (English): Everyone around me recommended a dishwasher, so I looked into it.
Comments (English): [ The dishwasher is really good. ] || ---------------- || Everyone around me recommended a dishwasher, so I looked into it. Since 6-place setting models are hard to find, I compared various options and decided to buy a Samsung one. First off, since it's a desktop model, I only needed to drill a small hole for the water hose, so no construction work was required. I was also surprised by how much bigger it was than I expected. I had been thinking about it for a year and keeping an eye on it, but while it was affordable until last year, the price suddenly skyrocketed this year. I was finally able to buy it at a mid-range price. I guess you really should just go for it when you're undecided. Using the dishwasher has been so convenient and great. I pre-wash the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher to run it. It takes about an hour and a half, so I pile up the day's accumulated dishes in the dishwasher for pre-washing and run it all at once in the evening. Then, the dishes are completely dry the next day, so I just have to tidy them up. It's so great and convenient. I really should have bought this sooner. Oh, and you have to be good at Tetris. I still don't have the knack for it, so I spend a lot of time thinking about how to fit everything in, haha. I saw a lot of reviews mentioning water stains after drying, but I think it depends on the detergent. Mine had absolutely nothing in it, and everything was clean and well-dried. For reference, I use Frosh Mini solid detergent. I heard that for the 6-person capacity, you absolutely must buy the Mini size so you only need to put in one tablet directly. I am planning for a second child soon, and I think it is great that it has a bottle sterilization function, so I don't need to buy a separate bottle sterilizer. I was a bit surprised when the transparent lid turned opaque after I put the baby cutlery holder in the dishwasher. I looked it up and found that you can't just throw any dishes in; there are items that are allowed and items that aren't. I hope you check carefully before putting anything in. Anyway, I made a good purchase in the 400,000 won range, which is a decent mid-range price. Oh, and regarding the delivered product... as shown in the last photo, the gap was defective, so I had to contact them and reschedule the technician, which was a bit of a hassle and annoyance. Their response was a bit... lacking. I won't go into detail, but aside from the product itself, the service wasn't great. I hope you get lucky with your purchase.

Since 6-place setting models are hard to find, I compared various options and decided to buy a Samsung one. First off, since it's a desktop model, I only needed to drill a small hole for the water hose, so no construction work was required. I was also surprised by how much bigger it was than I expected. I had been thinking about it for a year and keeping an eye on it, but while it was affordable until last year, the price suddenly skyrocketed this year. I was finally able to buy it at a mid-range price. I guess you really should just go for it when you're undecided. Using the dishwasher has been so convenient and great. I pre-wash the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher to run it. It takes about an hour and a half, so I pile up the day's accumulated dishes in the dishwasher for pre-washing and run it all at once in the evening. Then, the dishes are completely dry the next day, so I just have to tidy them up. It's so great and convenient. I really should have bought this sooner. Oh, and you have to be good at Tetris. I still don't have the knack for it, so I spend a lot of time thinking about how to fit everything in, haha. I saw a lot of reviews mentioning water stains after drying, but I think it depends on the detergent. Mine had absolutely nothing in it, and everything was clean and well-dried. For reference, I use Frosh Mini solid detergent. I heard that for the 6-person capacity, you absolutely must buy the Mini size so you only need to put in one tablet directly. I am planning for a second child soon, and I think it is great that it has a bottle sterilization function, so I don't need to buy a separate bottle sterilizer. I was a bit surprised when the transparent lid turned opaque after I put the baby cutlery holder in the dishwasher. I looked it up and found that you can't just throw any dishes in; there are items that are allowed and items that aren't. I hope you check carefully before putting anything in. Anyway, I made a good purchase in the 400,000 won range, which is a decent mid-range price. Oh, and regarding the delivered product... as shown in the last photo, the gap was defective, so I had to contact them and reschedule the technician, which was a bit of a hassle and annoyance. Sentence (English): The day has finally come to leave a review.
Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.

Sentence (English): I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. --------------------------------------------------
Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.

ㅠㅠ) 같은게 보인다 (세제를 쪼개도, 헹굼 추가해도 마찬가지예요...) 그래서 이중으로 세척하는 번거로움이 있다 ㅠㅠ (아기식기는 걱정되어 뜨거운 물로 한번 더 문질러서 헹굴때가 종종 있어요 ㅠㅠ)작동이 끝나고 그대로 두면 물이 전혀 마르지 않는다총평 : 우려했던 관리비 (전기세, 물세)는 식세기 전과 후에 큰 변화를 느끼지 못했어요~ (원단위까지 꼼꼼하게 따져보진 않았습니다 ^^;) 열풍건조가 되면 더 편하겠지만 자기전에 문열고 건조대 빼는게 저에게는 크게 힘들지 않아요~주방 사용공간은 좁아졌지만 오히려 정리정돈이 수월해지면서 주방이 깔끔해졌어요~ 아기식판틈에 보이는 하얀부분(잔류세제 의심)은 추가로 헹궈주는 번거로움은 견딜만 해요~ 세제 문제일수도 있으니 중간에 한번 바꿔보도록 하려구요~왜 주변에서 식세기를 추천하는지 알것같아요~ 저는 8년이나 늦었지만 다른분들은 오래 안걸리셨으면 좋겠네요 이모님 맞이하는 시간이요..^^식세기 구매 후에는 남편이랑 설거지 때문에 싸운적이 한번도 없어요~ 가족의 평화를 주었고 올해 가장 현명한 소비품이라고 해도 과언이 아니예요!!무엇보다도 저녁에 아기와 보내는 소중한 시간을 선물해준 정말 고마운 제품이랍니다~ 3개월간 사용하면서 느낀 솔직한 리뷰이니 현재 고민하시는 분들에게 도움이 되셨음 좋겠어요 ^^

Sentence (English): June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty.
Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.

ㅠㅠ) 같은게 보인다 (세제를 쪼개도, 헹굼 추가해도 마찬가지예요...) 그래서 이중으로 세척하는 번거로움이 있다 ㅠㅠ (아기식기는 걱정되어 뜨거운 물로 한번 더 문질러서 헹굴때가 종종 있어요 ㅠㅠ)작동이 끝나고 그대로 두면 물이 전혀 마르지 않는다총평 : 우려했던 관리비 (전기세, 물세)는 식세기 전과 후에 큰 변화를 느끼지 못했어요~ (원단위까지 꼼꼼하게 따져보진 않았습니다 ^^;) 열풍건조가 되면 더 편하겠지만 자기전에 문열고 건조대 빼는게 저에게는 크게 힘들지 않아요~주방 사용공간은 좁아졌지만 오히려 정리정돈이 수월해지면서 주방이 깔끔해졌어요~ 아기식판틈에 보이는 하얀부분(잔류세제 의심)은 추가로 헹궈주는 번거로움은 견딜만 해요~ 세제 문제일수도 있으니 중간에 한번 바꿔보도록 하려구요~왜 주변에서 식세기를 추천하는지 알것같아요~ 저는 8년이나 늦었지만 다른분들은 오래 안걸리셨으면 좋겠네요 이모님 맞이하는 시간이요..^^식세기 구매 후에는 남편이랑 설거지 때문에 싸운적이 한번도 없어요~ 가족의 평화를 주었고 올해 가장 현명한 소비품이라고 해도 과언이 아니예요!!무엇보다도 저녁에 아기와 보내는 소중한 시간을 선물해준 정말 고마운 제품이랍니다~ 3개월간 사용하면서 느낀 솔직한 리뷰이니 현재 고민하시는 분들에게 도움이 되셨음 좋겠어요 ^^

Sentence (English): June 13: Installed.
Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.

Sentence (English): July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center.
Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.

Sentence (English): July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed.
Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.

Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.

Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.

Comments (English): [ Bought with my own money, Samsung 6-place setting dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The day has finally come to leave a review. I wanted to use it thoroughly and leave a proper review based on actual usage. -------------------------------------------------- June 12: Purchased + 5-year 安心Care warranty. June 13: Installed. July 21: Leak occurred, reported to AS center. July 24: Service technician visited, replacement confirmed. July 31: Replacement completed. -------------------------------------------------- On Monday morning, I went to organize the dishes and noticed the bottom of the sink was soaked with water. Thinking something was wrong, I turned on the dishwasher and confirmed that water was dripping from the gap at the back, so I requested AS that same morning. The earliest visit took 3 days. Since there was no error code on the product itself, the technician had to completely disassemble the unit to check the symptoms. He said it was a case he had never seen before and that replacing parts would likely be difficult. He mentioned that exchanges are possible if the problem occurs within one month of installation, but unfortunately, since a month had passed, he would contact the head office to see if an exchange was possible. Fortunately, it was approved for exchange, so I received a new product and have been using it well ever since. (I didn't have much luck with the lottery, but I'm glad it was exchanged.) For the past ten days, I was back to the hell of washing dishes by hand, so I ate out quite often. --------------------------------------------------------------. We have been married for 8 years, and since we are a dual-income couple, we rarely ate at home, so we managed without a dishwasher. However, after our baby was born and I had to prepare meals for the baby regularly, the amount of dishwashing increased significantly. I thought, "I really need to buy one now. If I keep putting it off, my relationship with my husband will grow even more," so after holding out for as long as I could, I finally made the purchase. Even up until the day of payment, I was still hesitant. I had doubts: "Is it really a professional dishwasher?" and "If it runs for over an hour, doesn't it need much more water?" I think I delayed the purchase a bit longer because I was worried about maintenance costs. Thanks to a card discount, I bought it for around 400,000-450,000 won and also registered for the Safety Care service. Installation was done the next day (as expected from Coupang!), and two technicians came; unlike other reviews, they were very kind. Although it was possible to run the pipe through the gap without drilling, like with a water purifier, I opted to have a hole drilled because they mentioned that a reinstallation might be necessary if the water pressure dropped. The drilling took less than 30 seconds. There was no manual included, but they explained how to use it simply and easily after installation. I only use the Standard, Rapid, and Powerful functions, so I haven't had any major difficulties yet. Before the dishwasher arrived, I prepared the Frog Mini that everyone uses, and I tried running the dishwasher for the first time on the evening of the installation day. It used to take a while because I wasn't very good at Tetris, but after doing it every day, I’ve become incredibly fast now. I dislike the smell caused by food residue and the frequent cleaning of the strainer, so I pre-wash the dishes with cold water before putting them in (just enough to remove food scraps, leaving the grease on). Perhaps that is why the strainer cleaning alarm hasn't gone off yet, and there is absolutely no smell. Except for large pots and pans, it easily fits all the tableware for a meal for a family of three, including cooking, and the operating noise is comparable to everyday noise (it doesn't bother me at all when the TV is on in the living room or when I'm playing with my baby). Since the lid opens and hot steam escapes a few minutes before the dishwasher finishes, and moisture remains in that state for a day, I open the door wide and pull the drying rack outside before bed to maximize the natural drying effect, and then organize the dishes the next morning. (Smooth dishes and cups are completely dry, but moisture still remains in grooves or curved parts like food container lids, so I wipe them with a paper towel to finish.) Using a dishwasher for the first time was a bit unfamiliar, but I adapted quickly. Thinking, "This is why people call it a 'Do-Auntie'," I resented buying it so late, but at the same time, I congratulated myself for making the right purchase. I will summarize my thoughts after nearly three months. Pros: Dishwashing stress has disappeared (I used to multitask by washing dishes while cooking, but now I can just cook and use a lot of dishes without any burden; I just run the dishwasher at the end and I'm done!). My legs don't hurt as dishwashing time has shortened. The time my baby waits for me has decreased, and the time I spend playing with the baby has increased (I am so happy). I don't fight with my husband, I don't hate him, and he says his stress has decreased as well. Cons: The kitchen has become smaller. Whether it is an issue with the detergent or the dishwasher's cleaning power, I see white water stains (residual detergent?) in the small crevices (it is the same even if I break the detergent packet or add an extra rinse). Therefore, there is the hassle of double-washing (I am worried about the baby's dishes, so I often scrub them one more time with hot water before rinsing). If left as is after the cycle ends, the water does not dry at all. Overall review: I didn't notice any significant change in the maintenance costs (electricity, water) before and after getting the dishwasher, which I was worried about. (I didn't calculate it meticulously down to the unit of currency ^^;) It would be more convenient if it had a hot air dryer, but opening the door and taking out the drying rack before bed isn't a big hassle for me. Although the usable kitchen space has shrunk, organizing has actually become easier, making the kitchen look much neater. The extra hassle of rinsing the white spots visible in the crevices of the baby's food tray (suspected to be residual detergent) is bearable. It might be a detergent issue, so I plan to try switching it out sometime. I understand now why people recommend dishwashers. I was 8 years late, but I hope it doesn't take others that long—not the time spent welcoming a dishwasher. Since buying the dishwasher, my husband and I haven't fought once over the dishes. It has brought peace to our family, and it is no exaggeration to say it is the smartest purchase of the year! Above all, it is a truly grateful product that gifted me precious time to spend with my baby in the evenings. This is an honest review based on my experience using it for 3 months, so I hope it helps those who are currently considering buying one.
